prompt.context: Your client is an online automotive marketplace that enables dealers and individuals to buy and sell cars. They have recently acquired 4 companies operating in a similar domain that have somewhat overlapping products. They are increasingly facing problems with their sales and service processes because of the acquisitions.
prompt.question: What should they do?

clarifying_info.a: Car dealers of different sizes — some spending a lot and some spending very little.

clarifying_info.q: How does the sales force currently serve dealers?
clarifying_info.a: The sales force meets all dealers face-to-face, irrespective of size.

clarifying_info.q: What types of products does the client offer?
clarifying_info.a: The client has media products (banners, etc.) and software products. Software products enable dealers to acquire a fleet of cars, merchandise/organize information about those cars, and put ads of those cars on websites.

clarifying_info.q: How exactly was the problem caused?
clarifying_info.a: The client was already serving the entire value chain through its own products. Through the acquisitions, the client added companies to its portfolio that made similar products and sold them to dealers — resulting in overlapping and duplicative offerings.

exhibits.title: Revenue Drivers — Dealer Counts
exhibits.shows: A table showing the net number of dealers, number of dealers added, and number of dealers lost for three divisions (A, B, C) — with figures for the 'without recommendations implemented' scenario and blank '?' cells for the 'with recommendations implemented' scenario.

exhibits.title: Average Annual Spend Per Dealer
exhibits.shows: A table showing the average annual spend per dealer (USD) for each division, comparing without recommendations and with recommendations implemented.

exhibits.title: Cost Drivers
exhibits.shows: A table listing cost driver categories and the incremental cost (increase or decrease in USD) due to recommendation implementation.

framework: Diagnose root causes of sales and service problems post-acquisition (overlapping products, sales force structure, IT systems, dealer segmentation)
Identify solutions for each root cause (product rationalization, sales incentives, IT integration, sales force redesign, dealer segmentation)
Assess risks of each solution and propose mitigation strategies
Quantify financial impact of recommendations (EBITDA: revenue uplift minus cost increases)

questions.prompt: What do you think is causing the problems in the sales and service functions?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify multiple root causes: (1) Similar/overlapping products from acquired companies create internal confusion and cannibalization; (2) Sales force lacks incentives to cross-sell or up-sell products from acquired companies; (3) No robust centralized IT system — no single view of what is sold to whom; (4) Too many sales roles creating confusion around roles and responsibilities; (5) Disproportionate time spent serving low-value dealers in person.

questions.prompt: What solutions would you recommend for each root cause?
questions.guidance: For each root cause, a strong answer maps a specific solution: (1) Overlapping products → product bundling and/or killing redundant products; (2) Cross-sell/up-sell gap → redesign sales force incentives to reward cross-sell and up-sell; (3) IT fragmentation → implement a centralized IT system with full visibility into accounts and products sold; (4) Role confusion → streamline and clearly define sales roles and responsibilities; (5) Dealer size mismatch → improve dealer segmentation and serve lower-spend dealers remotely rather than in person.

questions.prompt: What are the key risks associated with implementing these solutions?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates identify risks tied to each solution: (1) Dealer confusion or backlash if a product they value is killed; (2) Sales force may lose focus due to broadened responsibilities; increased turnover risk; (3) Centralized IT system may be costly and complex to implement; (4) Sales force restructuring may cause job losses, distrust, and reduced morale; (5) Changing the service model (remote vs. in-person) may cause dealer churn.

questions.prompt: How can these risks be mitigated?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose concrete mitigation: (1) Educate both sales force and dealers about the expected benefits of the changes; (2) Open dedicated remote service centers to maintain or improve dealer service quality while reducing cost; (3) Phase the IT implementation to manage cost and complexity; (4) Provide transition support and clear communication to the sales force.

questions.prompt: Estimate the financial impact of implementing all recommendations. Calculate the EBITDA impact.
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure this as: EBITDA impact = Revenue impact minus Cost impact. They should brainstorm revenue drivers (dealer growth, reduced churn, higher spend per dealer) and cost drivers (sales cost up, service cost down, IT cost up, other costs up), then use Exhibit 1, 2, and 3 to compute. Revenue drivers increase; net EBITDA impact is positive.

math.setup: Step 1: Compute net dealers with recommendations for each division using: Net dealers (with reco) = Net dealers (without reco) - Dealers lost (without reco) + Dealers lost (without reco) [already gone] + Dealers added (with reco) - Dealers lost (with reco). Simplified: Net (with reco) = Prior net + New adds (with reco) - New losses (with reco). Step 2: Compute revenue without and with recommendations. Step 3: Compute incremental revenue. Step 4: Compute incremental cost from Exhibit 3. Step 5: EBITDA impact = incremental revenue - incremental cost.
steps: Net dealers with reco: Division A = 90 - 5 + 20 - 0 = 100 (net change: lost 5 old, add 20 new, lose 0); Division B = 40 - 7 + 15 - 2 = 50 (net change: lost 7 old, add 15 new, lose 2); Division C = 45 - 2 + 10 - 2 = 50 (net change: lost 2 old, add 10 new, lose 2) [Note: formula per casebook = prior net - prior lost + prior added_with_reco - lost_with_reco: A=90-5+5+20-0=100 per interviewer copy showing 90-15+5+20-0=100 i.e. roll-forward from scratch: start=0+net90, then remove prior-year churn and add new]
Revenue without reco: Div A = 90 x $80,000 = $7.2M; Div B = 40 x $90,000 = $3.6M; Div C = 45 x $100,000 = $4.5M; Total = $15.3M
Revenue with reco: Div A = 100 x $90,000 = $9.0M; Div B = 50 x $100,000 = $5.0M; Div C = 50 x $110,000 = $5.5M; Total = $19.5M

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key revenue drivers and cost drivers that will be affected by implementing the recommendations? Will each driver increase or decrease?

categories.name: Revenue Drivers (all increase)
ideas: Increased dealer growth — more dealers added across all divisions due to better products and service
Reduced dealer churn — fewer dealers lost, especially in divisions where churn was high
Increased average spend per dealer — cross-sell and up-sell from bundled products drives higher revenue per account

categories.name: Cost Drivers
ideas: Sales costs increase — restructuring and new incentive programs require investment
Service costs decrease — remote service model reduces cost of serving low-value dealers
IT costs increase — implementing a centralized IT system requires upfront and ongoing investment
Other costs increase — change management, training, and integration expenses

recommendation: Rationalize the overlapping product portfolio through bundling and selective product elimination to reduce dealer and sales force confusion
Redesign sales force incentives to reward cross-sell and up-sell of the full product suite, and streamline roles and responsibilities
Implement a centralized IT system to provide full visibility into dealer accounts and products sold across all divisions
Segment dealers by spend and shift low-value dealer service to remote/dedicated service centers to free up sales capacity
Expected EBITDA impact of implementing all recommendations is approximately USD 3 million
risks: Dealer churn if valued products are eliminated; some dealers may resist bundling
Sales force resistance, distrust, or attrition due to role changes and new incentive structures
IT implementation may be costly, time-consuming, and disruptive
Changing the service model for smaller dealers may cause churn if not managed carefully
next_steps: Educate sales force and dealers on the benefits of the new model before rollout
Pilot remote service model in one region before full-scale deployment
Phase IT implementation with clear milestones to manage cost and risk
Monitor dealer churn and sales force turnover closely during transition
